title: Heads: fourteen ways of looking
note: text = subtitles; say = spelled for the voice. Head data from build/data/heads_data.json (capture_heads.py on Modal CPU); config from brain3d/trace.json model_card.

blocks.text: One attention pattern can only look one way. If it spends its weight on Manchester, little is left for battery, or for the word just before.
blocks.say: One attention pattern can only look one way. If it spends its weight on Manchester, little is left for battery, or for the word just before.

blocks.text: So the model splits the job. The 896 numbers are cut into 14 heads of 64. Each head asks its own question, and all 14 run at the same time.
blocks.say: So the model splits the job. The eight hundred and ninety-six numbers are cut into fourteen heads of sixty-four. Each head asks its own question, and all fourteen run at the same time.

blocks.text: To save memory, the heads share their keys and values. Fourteen queries, two sets of keys and values: seven heads to each set.
blocks.say: To save memory, the heads share their keys and values. Fourteen queries, two sets of keys and values: seven heads to each set.

blocks.text: So what do real heads do with Emma's question? Block 9, head 7, looks one step back. On average, each position puts 84 percent of its weight on the token just before it.
blocks.say: So what do real heads do with Emma's question? Block nine, head seven, looks one step back. On average, each position puts eighty-four percent of its weight on the token just before it.

blocks.text: Block 12, head 13, puts all of its weight on the very first token. It has nothing to add here, so it rests.
blocks.say: Block twelve, head thirteen, puts all of its weight on the very first token. It has nothing to add here, so it rests.

blocks.text: Block 24, head 2, looks for the place. From the last position, 65 percent lands on Manchester.
blocks.say: Block twenty-four, head two, looks for the place. From the last position, sixty-five percent lands on Manchester.

blocks.text: Block 19, head 13, reads Emma's question: 80 percent on her words, and 36 on stores.
blocks.say: Block nineteen, head thirteen, reads Emma's question: eighty percent on her words, and thirty-six on stores.

blocks.text: And when the model is about to write its number, block 2, head 7, looks at the only digits in the prompt: the date. 17 percent of its weight lands on the digits of 26 October 2026.
blocks.say: And when the model is about to write its number, block two, head seven, looks at the only digits in the prompt: the date. Seventeen percent of its weight lands on the digits of twenty-six October twenty twenty-six.

blocks.text: Each head hands back 64 numbers. Fourteen of them, side by side, make 896 again. The output matrix mixes them into one vector, and it is added to the column.
blocks.say: Each head hands back sixty-four numbers. Fourteen of them, side by side, make eight hundred and ninety-six again. The output matrix mixes them into one vector, and it is added to the column.

blocks.text: Fourteen heads in each of 24 blocks: 336 ways of looking, all in one pass.
blocks.say: Fourteen heads in each of twenty-four blocks: three hundred and thirty-six ways of looking, all in one pass.
